of: page-template.html § the diagram catalogue, report-format.md § Depth rules
notes: Not a section — a primitive that appears in several. Of the six kinds, TWO are CSS components and four are drawings, and the criterion is whose length is load-bearing: a kind is a component when the DIFF sets its size and a drawing when the CLAIM does. Section 4's figure is the .impact panel (cards stack per PR, lanes collapse at 780px) and a flow's PATH is a .pipe spine (as long as the chain it follows). So the first thing this case tests is that a run reaches for the COMPONENT where a component is right and does not draw an SVG out of habit — checks/diagram.rb will report `legend` and `box-json` as invented classes, but a run that hand-rolls the panel from .box and .edge passes every mechanical check while throwing away reflow and comparability. What checks/impact-paths.rb settles is the panel's shape; what it cannot settle is whether these are the RIGHT 2-3 paths and whether each edge is TRUE — and the cap is now tight enough that CHOOSING them is the work: a fourth consequence is not dropped by being left out of the panel, its entry is in the affected list and its explanation in the flow that owns it. That needs a reader. SECTION 2 HAS TWO DRAWINGS AGAIN and both are earned here: the boundary chain by monorepo-contract (serializer → JSON → type → hook → component, five stops, mismatch on the JSON→TYPE hop) and the guard fork by monolith-guard-chain (a changed filter condition, two request classes, and a gate the diverted one never reaches). The chain spent a design generation as a .pipe and that was half right — a component shows order fine and cannot show WHICH HOP, so real pages wrote the mismatch into a node, which is the .blast footnote failure in newer vocabulary. The failure to watch for now is the inverse: a run drawing the .pipe's own content as a linear SVG under the new licence. checks/behaviour-flows.rb fails a flow figure carrying neither .edge-dash nor .node-dead, which catches the flagrant version; the plausible version is a judged expectation. ER FRAGMENT AND LIFECYCLE ARE STILL UNEARNED BY EVERY FIXTURE HERE: rails-only-small adds one nullable column, monorepo-contract has no state machine, monolith-guard-chain changes no schema. Covering them needs a new fixture with a migration and a status enum; until then diagram.rb checks those two layouts against the template itself and nothing else does. What no script settles either way: whether the figure is TRUE, and whether it is legible. Run with --visual and look at the PNGs.

cases.expected_output: An .impact panel in section 4 whose chains run from the new column, through the unchanged query that scopes the selectable list, to what a user then sees, with a .legend naming all three node kinds. NO SVG at all: no lifecycle, because archived_at is a timestamp and not a state machine; no ER fragment for a single-column add; no boundary chain, because there is no client and so no field crosses anything; and no guard fork, because no gate's condition changed.
expectations: Section 4's figure is the .impact panel with a .legend, not an SVG — a run that draws it with .box and .edge has thrown away reflow and comparability while passing every mechanical check
Exactly the figures this diff earns: no lifecycle, because a nullable timestamp is not a state machine and drawing one would invent states the code does not have, and no ER fragment for one column

NO BOUNDARY CHAIN. There is no client here, so no field crosses a seam and there is nothing for a chain to draw. A restored catalogue layout is what a run reaches for out of habit, and this is the fixture where doing so invents a boundary
NO GUARD FORK. Adding a nullable column changes no gate's condition and creates no second request class, and a fork drawn here would invent a population the code does not distinguish
Solid border is changed, dashed is unchanged-and-affected, and the legend says which is which
The panel shows something the two lists cannot: the unchanged query sitting beside the changed column, as one frame rather than two sets

Where the finding is that something STOPS at a hop, the note under the panel says so in words — adjacency cannot express a directed edge, and this is the case where a run is most likely to reach for SVG instead
Read the PNGs from --visual if any SVG was drawn at all: nothing overlaps, no label leaves its box, and both themes are legible

cases.expected_output: A boundary-chain SVG for archived_at inside the flow that owns it, taken from the catalogue's 5-stop grid, with the mismatch marked on the JSON→TYPE hop, plus the .impact panel for section 4. No guard fork: this change is a contract, not a condition. Still no ER fragment and no lifecycle.
expectations: The crossing is drawn as the catalogue SVG at the 5-stop grid (x = 12/190/368/546/724), not as geometry of the run's own, and NOT with a narrowed viewBox — the scroller's child is min-width:880px, so a narrower canvas renders the whole figure larger than the page

The mismatch is marked on the HOP, with .edge-dash and a .t-edge label above it, and not written as a clause inside a box — writing it into a node is exactly what the component version produced and the reason the chain is a drawing again
The .pipe above it is the PATH — hook → route → controller → archive! → column — and the two are not two views of one thing. A flow carrying only one of them has lost either the route or the finding
The flow carries ONE figure. A primer, if it has one, does not count toward that budget: it is a brand badge, not a drawing

The strings are the fixture's own, not the specimen's. The sharpest mismatch here is the KEY RENAME — the wire carries archived_at, the type declares archivedAt, and nothing transforms between them — and it sits on the same hop as the nullability one, so a chain inheriting the specimen's `null vs. string` label has undersold the finding
The figcaption carries the search that confirmed no transform exists between the wire and the type; the drawing itself carries labels, not sentences
No guard fork: nothing here changes a gate's condition, and the diff creates no second request class
No ER fragment: one column plus its immediate neighbours does not earn one, and if the missing time_entries association is mentioned it is mentioned as ABSENT, which is the only reason to raise it
The dashed boxes in section 4 are exactly the unchanged consumers, selectableProjects and ProjectSelector, and nothing changed by the diff is dashed
Read the PNGs from --visual: nothing overlaps, the .edge-dash hop reads as the mismatch rather than as a broken connector, and both themes work

cases.expected_output: A guard-fork SVG inside the flow whose behaviour is gated: three gate rails, two named request classes, and the finding drawn as where the diverted class lands — a gate it never reaches, or a destination that sends it back. No boundary chain: this app is server-rendered, so there is no serializer and no generated type. No ER fragment and no lifecycle.
expectations: The fork is in the flow that owns the gated behaviour, not in a section of its own and not in section 5

The two tracks are the two populations the CHANGED CONDITION creates, named from the code rather than as abstract roles — a flag-only holder against an accepted role, or an invitee with an incomplete profile against a member

The diverted track ends where the code actually sends it, and any gate drawn .node-dead is one the request really never reaches. An edge that does not match the real filter order is worse than no figure, because it is followed

Where the destination re-enters the chain the figure CLOSES THE LOOP. A figure that ends the diverted track at a box has drawn a redirect as a destination, which is the one thing a numbered spine also cannot say and the reason this is a drawing
The .node-dead door carries a legend explaining the dashed treatment: unexplained, a dashed box reads as DELETED, which is the opposite of never evaluated
The negative: no fork for a guard that merely returns early for one class where that refusal is the intent. That is a field row, and drawing it invents a population the code does not distinguish

No boundary chain: no serializer, no generated type, no field crossing a wire. If a form-input-name → permitted-params → column crossing is drawn instead it takes the 3-stop grid, and it is the flow's ONE figure — not a second one beside the fork
The budget holds per flow: one drawing each, and a flow that appears to earn both a chain and a fork should have been two flows

Read the PNGs from --visual: the three gate names do not collide at 11px, the citation row clears the diversion horizontal, the .node-dead door's fill covers the rail behind it in BOTH themes, and the arrowheads land on their boxes rather than beside them
